seoTitle: Premium and Discount SMC: PD Array Matrix

metaDescription: Learn Premium and Discount in SMC using the PD Array Matrix: 50% Equilibrium, quadrants, array hierarchy, CE vs MT, suspension gaps and invalidation.
metaDescriptionUr: پریمیم اور ڈسکاؤنٹ SMC میں PD اَرے میٹرکس سیکھیں: 50% ایکویلیبریم، کواڈرنٹس، اَرے درجہ بندی، CE بمقابلہ MT، سسپنشن گیپس اور ان ویلیڈیشن۔
quickAnswer: Premium and Discount in SMC divide a completed trading range at its 50% Equilibrium midpoint. Prices above 50% sit in Premium (favored for sells), while prices below 50% sit in Discount (favored for buys). The PD Array Matrix ranks specific price structures—such as Liquidity Pools, Order Blocks, Fair Value Gaps, and Breakers—inside those two halves.
takeaways: Every Premium and Discount measurement depends strictly on a declared completed Dealing Range High and Low—switching anchors mid-move creates hindsight illusions.
Equilibrium (50%) divides expensive upper Premium (>50%) from lower Discount (<50%), with 25% and 75% Quadrant boundaries marking deep discount and deep premium.

The PD Array Matrix organizes nine specific chart references (Liquidity Pools, Mitigation, Breaker, Liquidity Void, FVG, Suspension/VI, Order Block, Rejection Block, and Time Gaps) by range side rather than treating every rectangle equally.
Internal Range Liquidity (FVGs and Order Blocks inside a range) and External Range Liquidity (old highs and lows at range edges) cycle back and forth across the Price Delivery Continuum.
Location alone never triggers a trade: always demand an opposing Draw on Liquidity, active London or New York session liquidity, LTF confirmation, and clear invalidation.

sections.title: 1. Why Traders Buy Expensive Tops & Sell Cheap Bottoms (Beginner Comic)

blocks.text: Imagine walking into an electronics auction where a laptop trades between $1,000 and $1,400 all month. At $1,360, shoppers rush in out of fear of missing out—only to watch prices drop right back toward $1,100 the next morning.

That exact emotional trap happens every day on candlestick charts. Impulse buyers chase green candles deep above Equilibrium (buying wholesale tops in Premium), while panicked sellers dump near the bottom shelf inside Discount. Step through the 4-panel auction story below to compare an impulse buyer against a patient PD Matrix planner.

sections.title: 2. Quick Answer: What Are Premium, Discount & The PD Array Matrix?

blocks.text: In Smart Money Concepts (SMC), Premium and Discount describe relative location inside a completed high-to-low price swing—never fundamental fair value of an asset. Equilibrium sits at the exact 50% midpoint: prices above 50% belong to the Premium half (studied for sells), while prices below 50% belong to the Discount half (studied for buys).

The PD Array Matrix (Premium/Discount Array Matrix) takes that two-shelf map one step further by organizing specific price-action references—such as Order Blocks, Fair Value Gaps, Breaker Blocks, Mitigation Blocks, Rejection Blocks, and Liquidity Pools—into an ordered hierarchy inside whichever half aligns with the higher-timeframe Draw on Liquidity.

blocks.title: Core Boundary Rule
blocks.text: Calling a zone 'Discount' or 'Premium' without naming both the Swing Low and Swing High anchors is meaningless. A price of 132 sits in deep Premium inside a 100–140 range (80%), yet sits in Discount inside a wider 100–180 range (40%).

sections.title: 3. Anatomy of a Dealing Range: Equilibrium (50%) & Quadrant Math (3D Cinema)

blocks.text: Before labeling a single Order Block or Fair Value Gap, define the active Dealing Range (also called a price leg or lookback interval). Take the completed Swing Low and completed Swing High and split the vertical distance into four equal quarters (25% increments):

rows: Upper External Range Liquidity boundary; target for longs or sweep origin for shorts
Deep Premium zone; houses OTE (0.62–0.79 bearish) and prime bearish PD arrays
Moderate Premium zone directly above 50% Equilibrium
Exact midpoint dividing Premium and Discount: (Range_High + Range_Low) ÷ 2
Moderate Discount zone directly below 50% Equilibrium
Deep Discount zone; houses deep bullish OTE and prime bullish PD arrays
Lower External Range Liquidity boundary; target for shorts or sweep origin for longs

sections.title: 4. How to Anchor a Dealing Range Properly (Without Hindsight Bias)

blocks.text: Beginners frequently lose consistency not because Equilibrium math fails, but because they secretly slide their range High or Low after a trade misses. Follow three strict anchoring rules:

items: Wait for Confirmed Endpoints: Never freeze a 0% or 100% boundary while price is still expanding aggressively without a swing confirmation.
Measure Current Price Without Cherry-Picking: Once a completed 20-day lookback or clear displacement impulse locks High and Low, calculate depth strictly from those frozen endpoints.

Record Extension Triggers Upfront: If price breaks cleanly above the High or below the Low on a closing basis, recognize an expanded dealing range—never retroactively change anchors to pretend a failed entry was 'never Discount'.

blocks.text: Time-windowed lookback models measure the past 20, 40, or 60 completed trading sessions (excluding weekends and market holidays) rather than calendar days. This ensures every session contributes true executed price discovery.

sections.title: 7. The Complete PD Array Inventory Ranked From External to Internal

sections.title: 8. The Premium PD Array Matrix Stack (Selling Above 50% Equilibrium)

blocks.text: When higher-timeframe narrative is bearish and price retraces above the 50% Equilibrium line into Premium, an analyst scans upward from Equilibrium toward the Range High in an orderly ladder:

items: Step 1 — Check Immediate Equilibrium Overhang: Inspect any Volume Imbalance, Suspension Body-Gap, or Bearish Fair Value Gap (SIBI) resting right above 50%.

Step 2 — Inspect Mid-to-Upper Premium Structures (60%–85%): Locate unmitigated Bearish Order Blocks (consecutive up-close run before a sharp sell-off), Breaker Blocks (failed bullish OBs after a sweep), or Mitigation Blocks inside the 0.62–0.79 OTE pocket.
Step 3 — Check Deep Extreme Boundaries (85%–100%): Mark Bearish Rejection Blocks (long upper wicks) and Buy-Side Liquidity (BSL / Old Highs) sitting near the top shelf of the range.
Rule of Alignment: An unmitigated Premium array paired with a fresh lower-timeframe shift carries far cleaner context than selling blindly into the very first small tick above 50%.

sections.title: 9. The Discount PD Array Matrix Stack (Buying Below 50% Equilibrium)

blocks.text: Flip polarity when higher-timeframe structure points upward toward untouched Buy-Side Liquidity and price pulls back below the 50% Equilibrium line into Discount:

items: Step 1 — Scan Just Under 50% Equilibrium: Spot immediate Bullish Fair Value Gaps (BISI), Volume Imbalances, or Suspension gaps sitting in the 25%–50% Upper Discount quarter.
Step 2 — Prioritize Deep Discount Confluence (0%–25% / Q1): Look for Bullish Order Blocks, Bullish Breaker Blocks, or Mitigation Blocks overlapping the 0.62–0.79 OTE window.
Step 3 — Watch Deep Extreme Boundaries (0%–10%): Identify Bullish Rejection Blocks (long lower wicks) and Sell-Side Liquidity (SSL / Old Lows) that price may sweep just prior to reversing higher.
Avoid Catching Falling Knives: Wait for price to tap an active Discount array and display a structural slowdown or lower-timeframe shift before assuming the pullback has ended.

sections.title: 10. Classic Wick FVG vs. Suspension Body-Gap vs. IFVG vs. Reclaimed Blocks

blocks.text: Not every gap-like candle formation obeys the same geometry. Confusing body gaps with classic outer-wick Fair Value Gaps—or failing to track whether a block flipped polarity—corrupts backtesting logs:

rows: Gap strictly between Candle 1 outer wick and Candle 3 outer wick across Candle 2
Primary BISI (bullish) or SIBI (bearish) imbalance; midpoint is Consequent Encroachment (50% CE).
Previous close = 100, central candle open/close = 102/106, next open = 108 leaving body gaps at 100–102 and 106–108 even if wicks touch
Must NEVER be labeled a classic 100–108 outer-wick FVG; measures body-price discontinuities separately.
An existing FVG whose entire range is closed cleanly through by an opposing candle body
Flips directional use: a broken bullish BISI can act as overhead bearish resistance (and vice versa).
A reference that acted in Direction A, failed temporarily (role shift), then was swiftly reclaimed back to Direction A
Tracks full sequence history rather than wiping out an original zone permanently.

sections.title: 11. Refining Any PD Array: 50% Consequent Encroachment (CE) vs. Mean Threshold (MT)

blocks.text: Beginners often ask whether to enter at the near edge of a PD array or wait for the middle. Inside SMC, two distinct precision midpoints separate gap structures from solid candle bodies:

rows: Fair Value Gaps, Liquidity Voids, NWOG/NDOG, Rejection Wicks
(Gap_High + Gap_Low) ÷ 2 (exact 50% midpoint of the gap or wick span)
Candle bodies ideally respect CE; full body closes cleanly past CE signal deeper traversal.
Order Blocks, Breaker Blocks, Mitigation Blocks
(OB_Body_Open + OB_Body_Close) ÷ 2 (exact 50% midpoint of the candle body/run)
Healthy Order Blocks often reject around the opening price or hold bodies above/below 50% MT.

sections.title: 13. Time-Based PD Arrays: NWOG, NDOG, Midnight Open & RTH Opening Gaps

blocks.text: Not every PD array is drawn from an intraday candle cluster. Time-anchored opening benchmarks carry heavy reference weight across weekly and daily rotations:

items: New Week Opening Gap (NWOG): Span between Friday 17:00 NY futures close and Sunday 18:00 NY reopen. NWOGs above current price sit in Premium; NWOGs below sit in Discount.
New Day Opening Gap (NDOG): Span between the prior weekday 16:59 M1 close (17:00 NY) and the 18:00 NY electronic reopen. Keeps weekday maintenance breaks distinct from RTH sessions.

Midnight Open (00:00 NY): Acts as a horizontal daily equilibrium benchmark—bullish daily sessions often dip below Midnight Open (Discount) before expanding higher, while bearish sessions rally above it (Premium) before dropping.
RTH Opening Gap (09:30 NY): Span between prior regular-hours 16:00 NY close and current 09:30 NY equity open.

sections.title: 14. The Price Delivery Continuum: How Internal & External Liquidity Cycle

blocks.text: Markets do not travel randomly between arbitrary lines; price oscillates purposefully between two complementary poles: External Range Liquidity (ERL — old swing highs and lows at range boundaries) and Internal Range Liquidity (IRL — FVGs, Order Blocks, and Breakers resting inside the range).

After price sweeps an External Swing High or Low (ERL), it frequently rebalances inward to an Internal FVG or Order Block (IRL). Once that internal array confirms reaction, price launches back outward toward the opposite External Liquidity pool. Step through the animated continuum diagram below to see both legs connect cleanly.

blocks.text: Even an ideal Discount Order Block behaves differently depending on the resistance standing between your entry and the opposing Draw on Liquidity:

rows: Clean displacement legs with stacked unmitigated FVGs and crisp untouched old highs/lows ahead
Price glides swiftly between Discount IRL and Premium ERL; shallow pullbacks may skip deep arrays
Wait for confirmed shallow IRL (FVG/VI) rather than demanding an untouched 0.79 extreme
Overlapping choppy wicks, prior broken FVGs, conflicting news spikes, and dense swing clusters overhead
Price stalls repeatedly against opposing PD arrays, creating false breakouts and deep stop hunts
Demand strict multi-gate confluence or stand aside cleanly during consolidation

sections.title: 17. Multi-Timeframe Nesting: How a 15M Premium Fits Inside a Daily Discount

blocks.text: Here is the #1 confusion that trips up intermediate traders: 'If Daily says Discount, why does my 15M range say Premium?' Because Dealing Ranges are fractal! Every timeframe owns its own High-to-Low boundary.

When a market pulls down into a 4H Discount Order Block, a small bounce on the 15M chart can briefly look like '15M Premium'. Instead of fighting the 4H Discount narrative with blind shorts, patient traders wait for that tiny 15M swing to finish dipping back into 15M Discount—aligning Weekly, Daily/4H, and 15M/5M Discount simultaneously. Click the three fractal clocks below to inspect this nesting visually.

sections.title: 18. Intermediate-Term Highs/Lows & Structural Confirmation Delay

blocks.text: Advanced PD Array mapping often pairs structural swings with PD context—for instance, identifying an Intermediate-Term High (ITH) whenever a short-term swing high is flanked by lower short-term highs on both left and right sides, or when a short-term swing high forms inside a higher-timeframe Premium PD array.

blocks.title: Confirmation Timing Warning
blocks.text: Because the right-hand lower high arrives AFTER the central turning candle prints, an Intermediate-Term High is never fully confirmed at the top tick itself. Always log exact recognition time separately from hindsight turning labels.

sections.title: 21. Six Common Premium, Discount & PD Array Matrix Mistakes to Eliminate

items: Buying an 'Attractive FVG' Stuck at 80% Premium: Ignoring range half simply because a 1M FVG looks clean—leaving zero room before the Range High ceiling.
Anchor-Switching After a Loss: Changing a 20-day dealing range to a 60-day range post-trade solely to rationalize why a blown stop was 'really Premium.'
Selling Counter-HTF Into a Weekly Discount OB: Taking tiny 5M bearish setups straight into major higher-timeframe support without checking HTF location.
Treating Every Box as a Blind Limit Order: Stepping in front of violent displacement without waiting for an internal sweep or LTF MSS reaction.
Confusing Suspension Body-Gaps With Classic Wick FVGs: Misreporting wick-overlapping body gaps as pure unfilled outer-wick gaps in journal audits.
Ignoring High-Resistance Chop & News Spikes: Expecting clean textbook array bounces during thin lunch windows or right ahead of CPI, NFP, and FOMC releases.

sections.title: 24. Preserved Study Reference, Baseline Audits & Institutional Sources

blocks.text: Start with the most recent twenty completed trading days, not twenty calendar days. Mark the highest high and lowest low, then divide their interval into quarters. For a 100–140 range, equilibrium is 120 and quarter levels are 110 and 130. Price at 132 lies in the upper quarter of this selected range. Premium means above its midpoint; discount means below. Neither word means an asset is fundamentally expensive or cheap. The range anchors must remain visible because another valid range can change the classification.

Locate a higher-timeframe objective and the relevant quadrant before refining a PD array on a lower timeframe. If a fifteen-minute FVG spans 120–126 but its upper half has already been traversed, do not call the entire interval untouched. Examine completed five-minute and one-minute candles to see which sub-interval remains a candidate. Return to the higher timeframe when new candles complete. A forty- or sixty-day lookback can be a separately labelled extension in a running market; switching anchors solely to fit an entry is hindsight.

A classic FVG compares outer wicks. A suspension reference instead examines body-price imbalances around a central candle; overlapping wicks do not automatically remove that body-based configuration. For example, a previous close of 100, central open/close of 102/106 and next open of 108 leave separate body gaps at 100–102 and 106–108. That is not proof of a classic 100–108 FVG. An inverse FVG changes directional use after a stated failure; a reclaimed reference returns to an earlier role after another change. These labels describe different histories.

Suppose your completed range is 100–140 and a bearish study begins near 134. A nearby premium reference at 132–134 fits that location; a bullish gap at 106–108 belongs to another part of the range. Neither wins merely by looking cleaner. Record which reference was known, how it had previously traded, and what would end its proposed role. A balanced price range is an overlap of specified opposing intervals, not a guarantee of support. A low-resistance move may leave your chosen array unvisited; a crowded high-resistance path may justify no study entry.

Start with the range and objective, then identify the relevant PD array and its internal geometry. An order block selects a candle or consecutive run; its opening price, body midpoint and full wick are different boundaries. A breaker adds a prior swing sequence and changed role. A rejection block emphasises a body reference attached to a rejection wick. FVG, IFVG, BPR and suspension describe other configurations. The hierarchy organises questions rather than proving that one rectangle always outranks another. Use the linked foundational chapters to apply each exact definition before combining references.

Structural labels depend on relationships among confirmed swings. Under a common nested comparison, an intermediate-term high is a selected short-term high with lower short-term highs on either side; the exact convention must be stated. The right-side comparison arrives later, so the label cannot be known at the central high’s first print. A higher-timeframe PD array may give that swing context, but does not erase confirmation delay. Link the swing hierarchy to the range map without pretending a final structural label was available at the turning candle.
Keep the higher-timeframe map separate from lower-timeframe execution. Chart Laboratory is the place to practise recognising individual references before combining them into one model.

sections.title: 25. Frequently Asked Questions About Premium, Discount & The PD Array Matrix

blocks.text: Review clear answers to the twelve most frequently searched beginner, intermediate, and advanced questions on Premium, Discount, and the PD Array Matrix in SMC.

faqs.question: What does Premium and Discount mean in SMC trading?
faqs.answer: In Smart Money Concepts (SMC), Premium and Discount split a completed High-to-Low Dealing Range across its 50% Equilibrium midpoint. Any price above 50% sits in Premium (favored for sells), while any price below 50% sits in Discount (favored for buys).

faqs.question: What does PD stand for in PD Array Matrix?
faqs.answer: PD stands for Premium and Discount. A PD Array Matrix is an organized checklist ranking specific chart zones—such as Liquidity Pools, Order Blocks, Fair Value Gaps, Breaker Blocks, and Rejection Blocks—across the Premium and Discount halves of a range.

faqs.question: What is the exact 50% Equilibrium formula?
faqs.answer: Equilibrium equals the arithmetic midpoint of your chosen completed Swing High and Swing Low: Equilibrium = (Range_High + Range_Low) ÷ 2. Dividing that span further into quarters gives 25% Deep Discount and 75% Deep Premium levels.

faqs.question: Does Premium mean an asset is fundamentally overvalued?
faqs.answer: No. Premium and Discount in SMC describe purely relative price location inside a stated chart lookback window (such as 20 completed trading days). Changing the swing anchors changes whether the exact same price reads as Premium or Discount.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Internal Range Liquidity (IRL) and External Range Liquidity (ERL)?
faqs.answer: External Range Liquidity (ERL) sits at the outer Swing Highs and Swing Lows of your Dealing Range. Internal Range Liquidity (IRL) sits inside the range as Fair Value Gaps, Order Blocks, Voids, or Breakers. Price cycles systematically between IRL pulls and ERL sweeps.

faqs.question: What is the PD Array Matrix hierarchy order from strongest location upward or downward?
faqs.answer: From the interior outward, traders scan Liquidity Pools (Old Highs/Lows), Mitigation Blocks, Breaker Blocks, Liquidity Voids, Fair Value Gaps, Volume Imbalances / Suspension Blocks, Order Blocks, Rejection Blocks, and Time-Based Opening Gaps (NWOG/NDOG).

faqs.question: How does Consequent Encroachment (CE) differ from Mean Threshold (MT)?
faqs.answer: Consequent Encroachment (CE) marks the exact 50% midpoint of a gap or rejection wick (such as an FVG, NWOG, or NDOG). Mean Threshold (MT) marks the exact 50% midpoint of a solid candle body or consecutive candle run (Order Block or Breaker).

faqs.question: What makes a Suspension Block different from a classic Fair Value Gap?
faqs.answer: A classic Fair Value Gap measures non-overlapping outer wicks between Candle 1 and Candle 3. A Suspension Block inspects adjacent candle-body gaps flanking a central candle even when outer wicks overlap, so both configurations must stay separately classified.

faqs.question: How can price be in Premium on a 15-minute chart while sitting in Daily Discount?
faqs.answer: Dealing ranges are fractal across timeframes. Inside a large Daily Discount Order Block, a small upward 15-minute bounce may reach 75% of that tiny 15M swing. Patient analysts align all clocks by waiting for the 15M leg to pull back into 15M Discount before entering.

faqs.question: Should you trade a Premium or Discount PD array with blind limit orders?
faqs.answer: No. Reaching 25% Discount or 75% Premium only provides location context. Higher-probability discipline demands an opposing Draw on Liquidity, active London or New York session liquidity, lower-timeframe confirmation (MSS/CISD), and strict stop invalidation.

faqs.question: Why should you use 20 completed trading days instead of 20 calendar days?
faqs.answer: Weekends and market holidays record zero executed volume. Counting 20 completed trading sessions keeps lookbacks consistent across instruments and prevents switching randomly to 40-day or 60-day anchors after seeing outcomes.

faqs.question: What invalidates a Premium or Discount PD Array Matrix setup?
faqs.answer: A setup invalidates when price closes cleanly beyond the protective array boundary or past the anchored 0% Range Low (for bullish setups) or 100% Range High (for bearish setups), breaking the range thesis rather than shifting lookbacks after the fact.
